admission.justification: Holding a capture for a walk was a real alternative with a lifecycle cost; the rejection names the storage that would outlive its owner.

alternatives.option: Capture again on every page and refuse a continuation whose tree changed
alternatives.reason: No capture outlives its page, so a walk can never serve the rest of an anchor set from a tree the caller is no longer looking at.

alternatives.option: Hold one capture for the whole walk
alternatives.reason: It would keep scratch storage alive between two turns of an agent, across an unbounded interval and with no owner to close it.
alternatives.reconsider_when: a capture can be held cheaply across pages, or re-capturing a large worktree measurably dominates the cost of a walk.

consequences: `code_state` travels in the token, and an unchanged worktree yields the same tree id so the walk continues; a changed one is refused with the code-tree refusal.
context: A working-tree read captures the checkout into scratch storage. A walk spans several pages, so the packet had to decide whether a capture outlives the page that made it or is taken again.
decider: the developer, under D47, as MIK-R73@v1 rule 7 and inventory entry 151 state it
